question: Why did FeCoNiCrMn@CNTs adsorb more 2-CEES than pristine CNTs between 30 min and 30 h?
expect: premise false: in that period its apparent capacity stayed LOWER than pristine CNTs', attributed to concurrent catalytic degradation; it ends higher only at 48 h (636 mg/g) (sec. 3.2)
rendered:
Document: 3D network carbon nanotube film supported FeCoNiCrMn high-entropy alloy nanoparticles for integrated adsorption and detoxification of sulfur mustard simulant, page 3-6

Answer: The FeCoNiCrMn@CNTs composite exhibited a lower apparent adsorption capacity than pristine CNTs between 30 min and 30 h due to the coexistence of adsorption and catalytic degradation processes. The FeCoNiCrMn nanoparticles introduced multimetallic active sites that catalyzed the chemical transformation of 2-CEES, leading to partial degradation during the adsorption process. As a result, part of the adsorbed 2-CEES underwent catalytic conversion rather than simple accumulation, thereby reducing the net gravimetrically measured mass gain during this period.
